utility.notes: LG&E is Louisville's well-established dominant electric utility, operated jointly with Kentucky Utilities (KU) under the shared LG&E and KU Energy company.

value.name: Louisville Gas and Electric (LG&E)
value.notes: No Community Choice Aggregator was found serving Louisville's residential solar customers this session; LG&E is recorded as both the distribution and default generation utility.

county.notes: Louisville and Jefferson County operate a consolidated Louisville Metro government; Develop Louisville's Division of Construction Review is the single permitting authority for the whole consolidated jurisdiction.

permit_authority.value: Louisville Metro Government, Develop Louisville — Division of Construction Review
permit_authority.notes: The Kentucky Building Code is adopted at the state level by the Department of Housing, Buildings and Construction (DHBC), but enforcement is local — in counties/cities that maintain their own building department (like consolidated Louisville Metro), that local department is the AHJ; in smaller counties without a local building department, DHBC may enforce directly. Louisville's own Division of Construction Review is a genuinely consolidated authority for the whole Louisville Metro (city-county) government.

interconnection_url.notes: Per LG&E and KU's own page: net metering is capped at 45kW system capacity. Two credit structures apply depending on enrollment date: NMS-1 (enrolled before 2021-09-24) credits excess generation in kWh to offset future usage; NMS-2 (enrolled on/after 2021-09-24) credits excess generation in dollars at the Kentucky Public Service Commission's set rate (6.9 cents/kWh for LG&E, 7.4 cents/kWh for KU, effective 2021-09-24), carrying over as a bill credit but never paid out in cash. The 5-step application process (requirements review, application with 3 attachments via email or mail, review/approval, installation with inspections, utility meter installation/activation) is typically fee-free for nearly all applicants.

required_documents.notes: Per the City's own 'Installing Solar in Louisville' page, which links a downloadable permitting checklist. Electrical work must comply with Article 690 of the most recently adopted National Electrical Code edition.

value: After installation, an inspection is required and requested through Develop Louisville's Division of Construction Review 'Request an Inspection' webpage
Applicants must pass an electrical inspection (roof- and ground-mounted systems) and, for roof-mounted systems, a building inspection as well
Expect a wait of 3-4 business days for an inspection; times vary by staff workload and application complexity
Inspections are not guaranteed within the 3-day streamlined permitting turnaround window

value.notes: Per the City's own page: electrical permits are issued the SAME DAY a complete application is submitted (online applications receive a permit immediately). Simplified building permits for streamlined-eligible residential rooftop/ground-mount projects are turned around within 3 days or less when a complete package (including the licensed engineer/architect roof-support documentation) is submitted; most simplified building permits can be obtained the same day, with 4-5 business days anticipated for full review if not fully streamlined. Non-streamlined-eligible projects (and all commercial projects) instead require a full qualified review without the 3-day guarantee. No specific automated-review platform is named in the source material, so none is recorded here.

value.program_or_pathway: Streamlined 3-day permitting path for residential rooftop and ground-mount systems meeting completeness/engineering criteria
other_conditions: In residential districts, roof-mounted systems may not exceed 10 feet above the maximum height allowed by the underlying form district, and no system may be attached to a building's wall or side (per Land Development Code Section 4.3.16)
Freestanding (ground-mount) systems may not exceed the maximum building height of the underlying form district, and alternative-energy systems/equipment may cover no more than 25% of the lot area

Properties in a historic preservation district or Architectural Review Committee jurisdiction require a Certificate of Appropriateness; most ARCs discourage panels visible from a building's primary/street-facing elevation but will work with owners on placement
The 45kW figure recorded here reflects the statewide LG&E/KU net-metering capacity cap, not a separate City permit-eligibility limit

rebates.notes: The City's own page describes the federal 30% Investment Tax Credit (a statewide/nationwide incentive, not Louisville-specific) and the Energy Project Assessment District (EPAD) financing program (a loan-repayment mechanism for larger/commercial properties, not a rebate) — no specific Louisville-only rebate dollar amount was found, left null rather than conflating these with a locality-specific rebate.
